dlc.name: Fallen Ghosts
dlc.summary: Your helicopter is shot down during an evacuation and ex-US Special Forces mercenaries hunt your squad. Adds a new enemy, new skills and exclusive weapons.

resources_note: Type in the numbers from the top of your Skills menu. It saves automatically.

resources.name: Skill Points
resources.hint: From levelling up and Skill Point pickups.

weapon_skills.description: Weapon skill tree. Each skill has between 1 and 4 ranks; click a rank box to mark your current rank. A skill with a matching Bonus Medal also gets an independent star toggle for that medal. The Epic skill at the end unlocks once every other Weapon skill has at least 1 rank.

items.name: Stable Aim
items.guide: Reduces sway when aiming heavy sniper rifles.

items.name: Hip Fire Spread
items.guide: Tightens bullet spread when firing from the hip.

items.name: Grenade Launcher
items.guide: Unlocks an under-barrel launcher that fires frag grenades quickly. To use it: buy this skill, pick up a launcher attachment case in the world (the M203 is reported to be in the village of Poco in Remanzo), then open Gunsmith on a compatible assault rifle and fit it in the Underbarrel slot.

items.name: Ammo Capacity
items.guide: Lets you carry more reserve ammo (not more per magazine).

items.name: VHC Destruction
items.guide: Increases the damage your weapons deal to vehicles.

items.name: ADV Suppressor
items.location: Weapon Skill Tree · unlocks at Level 14
items.guide: Keeps full weapon damage while a suppressor is attached.

items.name: Time to Aim
items.location: Weapon Skill Tree · unlocks at Level 14
items.guide: Shortens the time it takes to aim scoped weapons.

items.name: Ammo Retention
items.location: Weapon Skill Tree · unlocks at Level 14
items.guide: Refills all carried ammo whenever you respawn.

items.name: Ranged Elite
items.guide: EPIC SKILL: Increases weapon accuracy at long range. Unlocks once every other skill in the Weapon tree has at least 1 rank.

drone_skills.description: Drone skill tree. Each skill has between 1 and 4 ranks; click a rank box to mark your current rank. A skill with a matching Bonus Medal also gets an independent star toggle for that medal. The Epic skill at the end unlocks once every other Drone skill has at least 1 rank.

items.name: Battery
items.guide: Extends how long the drone can stay airborne. The final rank gives unlimited battery.

items.name: Night Vision
items.guide: Improves the drone's camera for use in low light.

items.name: Range
items.guide: Extends how far the drone can fly from the operator before losing signal.

items.name: Speed
items.guide: Makes the drone fly faster and turn more nimbly.

items.name: Mark Area
items.guide: Lets the drone spot and mark targets across a wider area.

items.name: Stealth
items.guide: Reduces the noise the drone makes in flight.

items.name: Cooldown
items.guide: Shortens the wait before the drone's payload can be used again.

items.name: Noisemaker
items.guide: Lets the drone emit noise to distract and lure enemies.

items.name: Zoom
items.location: Drone Skill Tree · unlocks at Level 15
items.guide: Increases the drone camera's maximum zoom.

items.name: Explosive
items.location: Drone Skill Tree · unlocks at Level 15
items.guide: Equips the drone with a remotely detonated explosive charge.

items.name: EMP
items.location: Drone Skill Tree · unlocks at Level 15
items.guide: Equips the drone with an EMP charge that disables nearby vehicles and electronics.

items.name: Armor
items.location: Drone Skill Tree · unlocks at Level 15
items.guide: Lets the drone absorb more damage before being destroyed.

items.name: Thermal Vision
items.location: Drone Skill Tree · unlocks at Level 15
items.guide: Gives the drone a thermal camera mode.

items.name: Medic
items.guide: EPIC SKILL: A drone payload that detonates to revive nearby allies. Unlocks once every other skill in the Drone tree has at least 1 rank.

item_skills.description: Item skill tree. Each skill has between 1 and 4 ranks; click a rank box to mark your current rank. A skill with a matching Bonus Medal also gets an independent star toggle for that medal. The Epic skill at the end unlocks once every other Item skill has at least 1 rank.

items.name: Parachute
items.guide: Lets you deploy a parachute to land safely after jumping or falling from aircraft.

items.name: Binocular Zoom
items.guide: Increases the binoculars' maximum zoom level.

items.name: Mine
items.guide: Unlocks a proximity mine that damages infantry and vehicles; higher ranks carry more.

items.name: Diversion Lure
items.guide: Throws a lure that draws nearby enemies to a chosen spot.

items.name: Frag Grenade
items.guide: Unlocks frag grenades; higher ranks let you carry more.

items.name: C4
items.guide: Unlocks remote-detonated C4 charges; higher ranks let you carry more.

items.name: Binocular Recon
items.guide: Improves how quickly and accurately the binoculars identify and tag targets.

items.name: Thermal Vision
items.guide: Gives you a handheld thermal-vision mode.

items.name: Flashbang
items.guide: Unlocks flashbangs that disorient groups of enemies.

items.name: Flare Gun
items.guide: Fires a flare that draws enemy attention to where it lands.

items.name: Explosion Radius
items.guide: EPIC SKILL: Increases the blast radius of your explosives. Unlocks once every other skill in the Item tree has at least 1 rank.

physical_skills.description: Physical skill tree. Each skill has between 1 and 4 ranks; click a rank box to mark your current rank. A skill with a matching Bonus Medal also gets an independent star toggle for that medal. The Epic skill at the end unlocks once every other Physical skill has at least 1 rank.

items.name: Stamina
items.guide: Extends how long you can sprint before running out of breath.

items.name: No Pain
items.guide: Lengthens the damage-resistant window after being revived.

items.name: Car Shield
items.guide: Reduces weapon damage taken while driving a ground vehicle.

bonus.name: Car Shield
bonus.desc: Reduces incoming damage by 10% while driving.

items.name: Quiet Running
items.guide: Makes running quieter, so you're harder to hear while moving fast.

items.name: Bullet Resistance
items.guide: Reduces the damage you take from bullets.

bonus.name: Bullet Resistance
bonus.desc: 5% damage reduction. Found in Itacua (Bonus Medal #1): in a dirt-yard camp with tents and a helipad, on the ground beside the small concrete building.

items.name: Detection
items.location: Physical Skill Tree · unlocks at Level 17
items.guide: Makes you harder for enemies to spot while crouched or prone.

bonus.name: Detection
bonus.desc: Slows the enemy detection rate by 5%.

items.name: Explosion Resistance
items.location: Physical Skill Tree · unlocks at Level 17
items.guide: Reduces the damage you take from explosions.

items.name: Aircraft Shield
items.location: Physical Skill Tree · unlocks at Level 17
items.guide: Reduces weapon damage taken while piloting an aircraft.

bonus.name: Aircraft Shield
bonus.desc: Reduces incoming damage by 10% while piloting.

items.name: Faster Regen
items.guide: EPIC SKILL: Recover from injuries faster. Unlocks once every other skill in the Physical tree has at least 1 rank.

squad_skills.description: Squad skill tree. Each skill has between 1 and 4 ranks; click a rank box to mark your current rank. A skill with a matching Bonus Medal also gets an independent star toggle for that medal. The Epic skill at the end unlocks once every other Squad skill has at least 1 rank.

items.name: Revive Speed
items.guide: Speeds up how quickly you revive a downed teammate.

items.name: Extra Sync Shot
items.guide: Adds extra targets to your Sync Shot marks.

items.name: Trained Rebels
items.guide: Makes allied rebel fighters hit harder.

items.name: Squad Resilience
items.guide: Makes your AI teammates more resistant to bullet damage.

items.name: Bleed Out Time
items.location: Squad Skill Tree · unlocks at Level 16
items.guide: Extends how long you survive while waiting to be revived.

items.name: Born Leader
items.location: Squad Skill Tree · unlocks at Level 16
items.guide: Makes your AI teammates more effective overall.

items.name: Last Chance
items.guide: EPIC SKILL: Increases how many times your AI teammates can revive you. Unlocks once every other skill in the Squad tree has at least 1 rank.

rebel_support_skills.description: Rebel Support skills. Each skill has 3 tiers (Power 1, 2 and 3), and each tier takes 3 levels, so 9 boxes per skill. Every Rebel Op side mission you finish adds one level to that skill. Find Rebel Ops through intel, interrogating lieutenants or talking to civilians.

items.name: Vehicle Drop-Off
items.guide: Calls in Rebel forces to drop off a vehicle nearby. Power 1: an SUV; Power 2: an armored vehicle; Power 3: a helicopter.

items.name: Guns for Hire
items.location: Tier 1: A small group of rebels fights alongside you.
items.guide: Summons temporary Rebel fighters to fight alongside you; higher ranks bring more. Power 1: a small group of rebels; Power 2: a medium group of rebels; Power 3: a very large group of rebels.

tier_groups.text: A small group of rebels fights alongside you.
A medium group of rebels fights alongside you.
A very large group of rebels fights alongside you.

items.name: Mortar
items.guide: Calls in a Rebel mortar strike on a marked area. Power 1: a single-target mortar strike; Power 2: multiple mortar strikes on the target; Power 3: multiple mortar strikes over a wide area.

tier_groups.text: Multiple mortar strikes on the target.
Multiple mortar strikes over a wide area.

items.name: Diversion
items.location: Tier 1: A small group of rebels draws enemies away.
items.guide: Has Rebels stage an attack from another direction to draw enemies away. Power 1: a small group of rebels; Power 2: a large group of rebels; Power 3: the largest group of rebels.

tier_groups.text: A small group of rebels draws enemies away.
A large group of rebels draws enemies away.
The largest group of rebels draws enemies away.

items.name: Spotting
items.location: Tier 1: Rebels mark enemies in a small area.
items.guide: Has Rebels mark nearby enemies; higher ranks widen the detection area. Power 1: marks enemies in a small area; Power 2: marks enemies in a large area; Power 3: marks enemies in the largest area. Only marks enemies, not intel or objectives.

tier_groups.text: Rebels mark enemies in a small area.
Rebels mark enemies in a large area.
Rebels mark enemies in the largest area.

recommended_weapons.description: Community-favourite weapons by type, including the quietest picks for suppressed play, and where known the province to find them in. Locations and detection distances come from search summaries and have not been checked in game. Tick a weapon once you own it.

items.name: M4A1
items.location: Flor de Oro · At Armadillo Hunting Lodge · 📍 -19.7442, -60.9439
items.guide: All-rounder: fast fire rate, solid damage, and quiet with a suppressor. Stealth pick: among the quietest assault rifles when suppressed.

items.name: TAR-21
items.location: Montuyoc · Just southwest of Choza Padre · 📍 -18.0857, -66.4078
items.guide: Balanced rifle that works at close and mid range.

items.name: ACR
items.location: Media Luna · Just west of Combat Outpost · 📍 -13.6098, -64.6326
items.guide: Very accurate with good damage and steady handling in long fights.

items.name: MK17
items.location: Flor de Oro · Northeast of M.O.B. Jaguar · 📍 -19.6525, -61.2556
items.guide: Hard-hitting with long range; plays like a battle rifle.

items.name: HTI
items.location: Montuyoc · Just northeast of Montuyoc Training Base · 📍 -17.5462, -64.8745
items.guide: Highest-damage sniper; can take out vehicles and helicopters.

items.name: MSR
items.location: Montuyoc · Just east of Choza Padre Mine · 📍 -17.5096, -66.9808
items.guide: Bolt-action pick for clean long-range kills.

items.name: G28
items.location: San Mateo · Just southwest of La Carcel Del Pueblo · 📍 -15.0954, -64.3632
items.guide: Semi-automatic marksman rifle for quick follow-up shots. Stealth pick for suppressed marksman work at medium range.

items.name: MK14
items.guide: Semi-automatic marksman rifle for medium to long range. Stealth pick for suppressed marksman work at medium range.

items.name: Vector .45 ACP
items.location: Media Luna · Just east of F.O.B. Buitre · 📍 -13.4959, -64.125
items.guide: Close-quarters favourite: very high fire rate. Stealth pick: subsonic rounds keep it discreet; pair it with an extended magazine.

items.name: MK249
items.guide: 150-round magazine for suppression and convoys.

items.name: 5.7 USG (Lady Killer variant)
items.guide: Comes with a suppressor and fires fast. Stealth pick: quieter up close than most suppressed rifles; the 5.7 USG is reported audible only within about 47-50 m.

items.name: D-50
items.guide: .50-calibre sidearm that drops armoured targets in a shot or two.

items.name: MP7
items.guide: Stealth pick: one of the quietest SMGs; enemies are reported to hear it only within about 59 m.

items.name: PSG 9mm
items.location: San Mateo · Just west of San Mateo Base · 📍 -15.4452, -64.8017
items.guide: Stealth pick: players report an even shorter detection distance than other compact SMGs.

items.name: Scorpion EVO 3
items.location: Koani · Just northeast of Combat Outpost · 📍 -14.1341, -65.7301
items.guide: Stealth pick for close quarters with a suppressor, long barrel and angled grip.

items.name: R5 RGP
items.guide: Stealth pick: strong suppressed damage with clean handling.

items.name: M1911
items.guide: Stealth pick: one of the most recommended suppressed pistols.

items.name: P12
items.guide: Stealth pick: regularly mentioned as a quiet sidearm.

items.name: Whisper pistol
items.guide: Stealth pick: among the quietest handguns, reported audible only within about 47-50 m.

kingslayer_files.description: All 201 base-game Kingslayer Files across the 21 provinces, numbered the same way as the in-game province list: 138 Documents, 46 Legends and 17 Videos. Videos (Bowman briefings) unlock automatically from story progress. Each card says what's nearby and gives Lat/Long you can match on the in-game Tacmap or MapGenie. Files only appear on your map once you get close or visit nearby ? locations. The Whole Story trophy only needs the collectible documents. Operation Oracle (DLC) adds 12 more, not listed here.

trophy.name: The Whole Story
trophy.requirement: Collect all collectible documents; mission-granted 'Word of Sueno' videos are not needed.

items.name: #1 El Pulpo
items.location: Bowman Briefing · Southwest of Observation Post · 📍 -17.5936, -64.4567
items.guide: This Kingslayer File unlocks automatically after Bowman's briefing upon entering Barvechos for the first time. Accountant to the cartel, expert money-launderer. Southwest of Observation Post (Watches the rebels' movements). 📍 Lat -17.5936, Long -64.4567.

items.name: #2 Job Security
items.guide: Nidia Flores rants at El Boquita about El Pulpo coming to audit her books. She's sure the man will find something to use against her, or manufacture it if he must, and that will be the end of her - in more ways than one. At Outpost (Secures Nidia's Hacienda, North sector). 📍 Lat -15.9339, Long -65.3008.

items.name: #3 Money Talks
items.guide: El Sueño tells El Pulpo how to deal with Nidia Flores. While Pulpo thinks Nidia might be skimming cash from their operations, El Sueño trusts her. He just wants Pulpo to teach her how to clean up her accounting, no matter how dumb or rotten Pulpo thinks she may be. At Outpost (Personal warehouse of a top cartel member). 📍 Lat -16.7174, Long -64.731.

items.name: #4 Mining Accident
items.location: Picture Evidence · Just northwest of Barvechos Mine · 📍 -16.5397, -64.7391
items.guide: A Barvechos Newspaper article about an accident at the Barvechos Silver Mine. Six miners were crushed after a crane collapsed. Bolivian silver mines have been worked for over five centuries. It is said that a bridge between La Paz and Spain could be built with the bodies of those who lost their lives in those mines. Just northwest of Barvechos Mine (Produces 4,000,000 ounces of silver per year). 📍 Lat -16.5397, Long -64.7391.

items.name: #5 The Heist
items.location: Picture Evidence · Just west of Pucamayu · 📍 -16.7775, -64.509
items.guide: A Unidad report about the attack of a convoy by unknown assailants. The initial findings of the investigation point to an ambush set by a Bolivian rebel group known as the Kataris 26. Just west of Pucamayu (People here scavenge from the Barvechos dump). 📍 Lat -16.7775, Long -64.509.

items.name: #6 Santísima Nidia
items.location: Picture Evidence · Just south of Los Fisgones · 📍 -17.0054, -64.8011
items.guide: A religious image of Nidia Flores, aka The Beauty Queen. Used by Santa Muerte worshipers and pilgrims to attract the good graces of the Boney Lady. Just south of Los Fisgones (The huge Barvechos city dump). 📍 Lat -17.0054, Long -64.8011.

items.name: #7 Follow the Money
items.location: Picture Evidence · Just northwest of Barvechos · 📍 -16.6588, -65.1841
items.guide: A diagram exposing the money laundring scheme used by Santa Blanca in Barvechos. Possibly left by Pulpo's staff during their audit of Nidia Flores' operations. Just northwest of Barvechos (A city built to support silver mining). 📍 Lat -16.6588, Long -65.1841.

items.name: #8 Bible Page - El Pozolero
items.location: Picture Evidence · Just southeast of Barvechos Mine Quarry · 📍 -16.3071, -64.8384
items.guide: The Santa Blanca Drug Cartel is writing its own version of the Bible. This is the page for El Pozolero, the Avenging Hand of Santa Blanca Just southeast of Barvechos Mine Quarry (Largest open-pit mine in Bolivia). 📍 Lat -16.3071, Long -64.8384.

items.name: #1 El Cerebro
items.location: Bowman Briefing · West of Malpaso Farm · 📍 -16.7683, -60.7422
items.guide: This Kingslayer File unlocks automatically after Bowman's briefing upon entering Caimanes for the first time. Recruited by Nidia Flores, highly intelligent but crazy, he designs drug subs for the cartel. West of Malpaso Farm (A corn farm). 📍 Lat -16.7683, Long -60.7422.

items.name: #2 Health Disaster
items.guide: A news report about a mosquito-borne breakout of elephantitis that's disabled 20% of the population. NGOs could quickly fix this with antibiotics if the government hadn't kicked all the NGOs out at El Sueño's request. Just south of Ingani (A remote fishing and caiman-hunting village). 📍 Lat -16.5868, Long -59.3262.

items.name: #3 Meeting Minutes
items.location: Recording · Just north of Puerto Chico · 📍 -17.3758, -59.9033
items.guide: A couple of El Cerebro's assistants bitch about how no one can understand a thing he says. Just north of Puerto Chico (A fishing village occupied by the cartel). 📍 Lat -17.3758, Long -59.9033.

items.name: #4 Mayday
items.location: Recording · Just north of San Miguel Ruins · 📍 -17.1117, -59.3632
items.guide: The captain of El Cerebro's supposed super-sub calls in a mayday when he runs the boat aground. Just north of San Miguel Ruins (Remains of a colonial site). 📍 Lat -17.1117, Long -59.3632.

items.name: #5 Nidia Flores Narcocorrido
items.location: Recording · Just southeast of San Miguel Ruins · 📍 -17.18, -59.3082
items.guide: Part of El Chido's album for Santa Blanca, this is the corrido for Nidia Flores, la Reina de Belleza. Just southeast of San Miguel Ruins (Remains of a colonial site). 📍 Lat -17.18, Long -59.3082.

items.name: #6 Red October
items.guide: The blueprint of a submarine, likely annotated by Santa Blanca engineers. The cartel has been known to use modified versions of Russian submarines to smuggle cocaine to Florida through the tributaries of the Amazon and the Orinoco, and then through the Atlantic ocean. At Outpost (A logistics platform for the narco-submarine base). 📍 Lat -16.5267, Long -59.7061.

items.name: #7 Bolivia Buchon Blog
items.guide: Lymphaitic filariasis, or "LF", is a parasitic worm spread by mosquitos which causes swelling in the arms and legs of those suffering from the condition. Caimanes has been hit hard by the disease and according to Bolivia Buchon Blog, "only Santa Blanca has stepped up to help the locals". At Ingani (A remote fishing and caiman-hunting village). 📍 Lat -16.5559, Long -59.327.

items.name: #8 Job Opportunity
items.guide: "Do you want to join an industry leader in a growing line of business? items.name: #10 The Pantanal
items.guide: The Pantanal is the world's largest wetland, with more than 150,000 square kilometers shared between Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay. During the rainy season, nearly 80% of the floodplains are under water. The various ecosystems house a tremendous biodiversity, notably rare aquatic plants and caimans, whose teeth are used as talismans by locals. At Camargo Campsite (A caiman hunters' camp). 📍 Lat -16.7722, Long -59.5645.

items.name: #11 The Boy that Turned into a Lake
items.guide: People from the eastern village of San Ignacio de Moxos say that, a long time ago, local women could only use a small swamp to wash clothes and men had to go fishing miles away. One day, a young boy went to help his mother and as he walked into the water, he mysteriously disappeared. His mother ran in the village to seek help. When villagers reached the swamp, the boy was nowhere to be seen. Nowadays, the swamp has turned into a beautiful lake full of fish and clean water. At Child Hunt (A lone hut). 📍 Lat -17.7752, Long -59.4778.

items.name: #9 Religious Syncretism
items.location: Legend · Just southwest of Santa Muerte Sanctuary · 📍 -14.3505, -60.2647
items.guide: The main religion in Bolivia is Catholicism, although it is considered highly syncretic. It is a complex mix of native and foreign influences, both in germs of rites and beliefs. In their effort to convert indigenous communities, the first Catholic Missions led by the Spanish mixed native religious principles with Catholic teachings in order to promote Christianity. The plan then was to gradually eliminate indigenous beliefs, except it never really worked. Today, it is still common to honor both God and Pachamama in the same ceremony. Just southwest of Santa Muerte Sanctuary (The holiest place of Santa Muerte). 📍 Lat -14.3505, Long -60.2647.

items.name: #10 Cult of Santa Muerte (expansion)
items.guide: The Santa Muerte Cult has been rapidly growing over the past 15 years, gaining several million followers in Mexico, the USA, and parts of Central America. This can be credited to a popular belief that Santa Muerte grants miracles more easily than her Catholic 'cousins', but it is also due to the fact she embodies the identity and values of a growing number of poor Mexicans facing violence and struggling to survive in a brutal economy. At Pilgrim House (Housing for foreign Santa Muerte pilgrims). 📍 Lat -14.335, Long -60.5804.

Serpiente (Protects the Unidad penitentiary). 📍 Lat -20.7016, Long -60.6761.

items.name: #9 Green Cross
items.guide: It is said that a famous street in La Paz, la calle Jean, used to be haunted by spirits and creatures from the Underworld. Ghosts, goblins and demons would appear at night, scaring people or playing tricks on them. The legend goes that one day, a local inhabitant, tired of their mischiefs, hanged a green cross at the entrance of the street and called upon a priest to bless it. The cross still visible in calle Jean, and reports of ghosts and spirits have since stopped. Or have they? At Hoalaca Ruins (The ruins of a small hamlet). 📍 Lat -19.2636, Long -61.605.

items.name: #1 Nuevo Mundo
items.guide: If you spend enough time in Camino Inca (Inca Trail), locals will tell you about a legendary village built in the mountains by people left homeless or displaced by the drug war. The village is called Nuevo Mundo and though no one is able to put it on a map, it is said that its inhabitants have built grand structures out of the wrecks of planes that have crashed in the Andes. If you overlook the mountains at night, you might see the light beams of those there trying to blind the pilots, so as to crash their planes. At Crash Site (The old wreckage of a civilian plane). 📍 Lat -19.5988, Long -66.4525.

items.name: #2 Quantu Legend
items.guide: According to popular belief, the Illimani and Illampu mountains, the highest peaks of Bolivia, are two fallen kings turned into rock by the Earth Goddess. In ancient times, Illimani and Illampu waged a ferocious war on the Altiplano and died in combat, but their sons sought revenge, and the war continued until both sons died as well. Pachamama was so upset that she punished the fathers, making their stars crash on earth, where they formed what are now the Illimani and Illampu mountains. At Crash Site (The old wreckage of a civilian plane). 📍 Lat -20.3948, Long -66.5821.

items.name: #3 Tiahuanaco
items.location: Legend · Just north of Inca Ruins · 📍 -19.6967, -66.0898
items.guide: Tiahuanaco is a major Bolivian archeological site and the heart of the Tiahuanaco Empire that ruled over the region between 300 and 1000 AD. It is composed of different types of temples organized on a geometrical and astronomical pattern. The level of technological advancement and the means used to build these structures remain a mystery to archaeologists and scientists. The most famous monuments are the Gateway of the Sun, the Kalasasaya temple, the Akapana pyramid, and the subterranean temple. Just north of Inca Ruins (Remains of an Inca settlement). 📍 Lat -19.6967, Long -66.0898.

items.name: #4 Camino del Inca
items.guide: The Inca Trail refers to a wide pre-Columbian road system that extended from southern Colombia to northern Chile, including Ecuador, Peru, and Bolivia. It connected all the regions of the Inca Empire and was centered in El Cuzco, the capital town. It was more than 40,000 kilometers long, at altitudes ranging between 2,000 and 5,000 meters. After the Spanish conquest, the Inca Trail was gradually abandoned. These days, only a few short sections have survived, mainly used by indigenous peasants or trekkers. At Inca Road (Built by the Inca Empire six centuries ago). 📍 Lat -19.7807, Long -65.9666.

A few months ago, all its villagers disappeared overnight. No one has seen anything or heard of them ever since. Some people believe Santa Blanca snatched the entire village. The village has since been colonized by a pack of hounds and is referred to as "Dogtown". The legend goes that if you use a special whistle you can control the dogs. Just northeast of Yopil (The cartel kidnapped every villager here). 📍 Lat -16.5866, Long -63.6037.

items.name: #10 The Wiphala Flag
items.guide: The Wiphala is an indigenous emblem in the Andes. It is a seven-color flag with a checkered pattern, each color related to a natural or religious element. Its origin is confuding, and different versions exist, each depending on what part or ethnic group of the Inca Empire it represents. Since 2009, the Aymara version has officially become the dual flag of Bolivia along with the classic red, yellow, and green banner. It now stands as a symbol of ethnical diversity. At Santa Catalina Chapel (Protects the drivers). 📍 Lat -17.1596, Long -63.4381.

items.name: #11 Kallawayas
items.guide: A Kallawaya divinatory charm called "Chambi". The Kallawayas are traditional traveling healers from the northern region of La Paz that cure both physical and mental pains. The medicine they practice is a thousand years old (pre-Incan period) and based on the natural properties of plants, animals and minerals from the Andes. A typical 'consultation' includes music, dances and the use of talismans. They have their own language and cosmogony that have been acknowledged by UNESCO. At Shamanic Site (A traditional religious site). 📍 Lat -14.8804, Long -67.1011.

items.name: #12 Salt Teardrops of Giants
items.guide: The Aymara have a myth to explain the creation of the Salt Flats of Uyuni. They believe that, long ago, the volcanoes surrounding the Salar could walk, talk and even fall in love. The legend says that Tunupa, one of the tallest volcanoes, became pregnant and gave birth to a baby volcanoe, believing he was the father, abducted the child. Tunupa cried for a long time. Her tears blended with her mother's milk, and the mix poured over the arid land, creating the Salt Flats. At Salt Miner's House (A salt miner and his family live here). 📍 Lat -14.5506, Long -66.6779.

items.name: #13 The Train Cemetery
items.location: Legend · Just southeast of Train Cemetery · 📍 -14.8214, -66.9625
items.guide: Uyuni was once a boom town, playing the role of a transport hub for trains carrying minerals to Pacific Ocean ports. After the mid-1900s, mining activity slowly declined and the trains were abandoned outside of Uyuni, forming a strange train cemetery, lost among the beautiful but desolated landscapes of Uyuni Salt Lake. It is now a major tourist attraction. Just southeast of Train Cemetery (Abandoned locomotives from the 1940s sit here). 📍 Lat -14.8214, Long -66.9625.

items.name: #14 Petroglyphs
items.guide: Petroglyphs are ancient images carved on rocks that can be found all over the world. Bolivia offers some beautiful examples of it, mostly in the Andes and in the eastern lowlands. The rock art covers a wide variety of cultures and ages. It shows hunting scenes, groups of camelids, human figures, and mysterious forms. At A Prehistoric Site (A pre-Columbian archeological site). 📍 Lat -13.9127, Long -66.0996.

Just southeast of Outpost (Monitors road traffic). 📍 Lat -19.3936, Long -60.3304.

items.name: #9 Jesús Malverde
items.guide: Jesús Malverde is a folk saint and local hero in the Mexican state of Sinaloa. As far as the story goes, he was born Jesús Juarez Mazo in 1870 in Culiacán and earned a reputation as the "generous" bandit", stealing from the rich and distributing to the needy before being hanged by the local governor in 1909. The expansion of the Malverde cult is allegedly linked to the rise of Mexican drug cartels in the 90s, which are deliberately associated with Malverde's image as a public relations strategy. Just northwest of Isque (Partially burned by the huge forest fire). 📍 Lat -18.9973, Long -59.529.

items.name: #10 Che Guevara (1928-67)
items.location: Legend · Just northeast of Santa Elena · 📍 -18.7938, -61.2545
items.guide: Born in Argentina, Ernesto "Che" Guevara joined the Cuban revolutionary movement led by Fidel Castro in the late 1950s. After the Castro took power in 1959, Che decided to promote the anti-imperialist and communist revolution throughout the world. After a failed attempt in Congo, he tried his luck in Bolivia. Che had some initial success in early 1967, but he was soon crushed by the US-backed Bolivian Army. Che was captured and executed in October. Since then, he has been a romantic icon of the Revolution. Just northeast of Santa Elena (A farm village occupied by the cartel). 📍 Lat -18.7938, Long -61.2545.

items.name: #10 The Witches' Market
items.guide: The Witches' Market, or Mercado de las Brujas, is located in the heights of La Paz, Bolivia. Selling everything from talismans, aphrodisiac powders, and amulets, to soapstone figurines thrown in the fire for good luck, the Witches' Market is run by local witch doctors - known as Yatiri - who perform white or black magic ceremonies for a few Bolivianos. Most popular of all items are the dried llama fetuses which are buried under the foundations of many houses as an offering to the Pachamama. At Oso (Sometimes used by the cartel). 📍 Lat -20.3726, Long -60.1937.

items.name: #11 Bolivian Witchcraft
items.location: Legend · Just east of Pa Kollu · 📍 -19.5948, -59.6481
items.guide: Witches - known as Yatiri in Aymara language - are common in Bolivia where they are traditionally considered as go-betweens between men and gods. For centuries, people turned to them for cures, good luck, or for making important decisions requiring the intercession for the gods. Today, they still perform rituals - which often involve chewing coca and burning icons - destined to provide good health and luck, or harm to your enemies (using black, skull-shaped candles, coffins or even penises). Just east of Pa Kollu (The place to buy curses or shields from spirits). 📍 Lat -19.5948, Long -59.6481.

items.name: #12 Simón Bolívar (1783-1830)
items.guide: Simón Bolívar is the major figure of the Latin American wars of independence against the Spanish crown. Born into a wealthy family, he was influenced by the Enlightenment philosophers and the French Revolution. Trained as a soldier, he fought against the Spanish and their allies for more than two decades, gradually liberating what are now Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, and Bolivia, giving his name to the latter. He died in 1830, without being able to maintain the political unity of Latin America. At Bolivar Square (In memory of the great liberator Simon Bolivar). 📍 Lat -19.7591, Long -60.1088.

items.name: #10 Cult of Santa Muerte (origins)
items.location: Legend · At Los Críos de la Muerte · 📍 -20.137, -63.137
items.guide: The Cult of Santa Muerte appeared in the Mexico area during the pre-Columbian era. Natives honored a Death god and its female counterpart to secure their way into the afterlife. During the Spanish era and under Catholic influence, the cult saw the emergence of a female saint known as Santa Muerte. Though rejected by mainstream churches, it gradually became a popular cult for people looking for protection against misfortunes. She has become the favorite saint of outlaws and drug traffickers. At Los Críos de la Muerte (A gift from El Cardenal). 📍 Lat -20.137, Long -63.137.

items.name: #11 Cult of Santa Muerte (criminal practice)
items.guide: In essence, Santa Muerte is a syncretic religion that intertwines both Catholic and Pagan beliefs. It tends to attract followers disillusioned with the institutional Catholic Church and living on the margins of the law or outside of it. Criminals and drug traffickers in particular have openly worshipped her - the most famous of the being Gilberto Garcia Mena, a boss of the Gulf Cartel of Matamoros. Narcos frequently seek 'blessing' for their ammunition and weapons or protection for their illegal ventures. North of Chacori Farm (A sheep-breeding farm). 📍 Lat -19.4844, Long -62.7187.

A wave of cartel murders forced General Baro, leader of Unidad, to make a deal with El Sueño: Unidad lets Santa Blanca operate as long as no blood is shed and no cocaine is sold domestically. North of Acevedo (The center of beef breeding in Media Luna). 📍 Lat -14.4187, Long -64.8076.

At Checkpoint (Controls road traffic). 📍 Lat -13.874, Long -64.2352.

items.name: #7 Illapa
items.guide: Illapa was the god of thunder and rain in Inca mythology. He is considered one of the most powerful gods of the Inca pantheon, along with Inti, the Sun god. He was often represented as a man wearing shiny clothing, a sling and a club. Ancient Incas believed that Illapa brought rain by drawing water from the Milky Way and pouring it over the earth. Thunder was the sound of his sling, and lightning was believed to be the gleam of his clothes. At Chipaya Farm (A coffee farm). 📍 Lat -13.9964, Long -64.087.

items.name: #8 The Devil's Bridge
items.location: Legend · At El Puente del Diablo · 📍 -13.8981, -64.2822
items.guide: As the legend goes, a young man was long ago requested to gather a large sum of money as a dowry to marry the girl he loved. When he finally rounded up the money, he rushed to join his lover, but got blocked by a river. So he made a pact with the devil: the devil agreed to build a bridge in exchange for his soul. However, as the bridge was nearly over, the young man changed his mind and summoned God to chase the devil away. Since then, an unfinished bridge stands over the river. At El Puente del Diablo (A ruined bridge). 📍 Lat -13.8981, Long -64.2822.

items.name: #9 Inca Dynastic War
items.guide: The sling was the traditional weapon used by Inca warriors during the Dynastic War which divided the Inca Empire between 1527 and 1532. Following Emperor Huayna Capac's death, two of his sons, Huáscar and Atahualpa, waged a war over who would succeed him. The conflict resulted in Atahualpa killing his brother and conquering the emperor title in 1532. His reign was shortened by the Spanish conquistadores led by Pizarro, who captured and executed him in 1533, marking the end of the Inca Empire. At Archaeology Site (A small camp for an archaeological dig). 📍 Lat -14.6863, Long -64.2861.

items.name: #8 Chullpas
items.guide: Chullpas are pre-Columbian stone funerary towers that can be found in the Andes of Bolivia and Peru. They were built to protect and honor the mummified bodies of noble family members. Along with some personal belongings, the corpses were placed inside in a fetal position. The door is usually facing East, so every morning the rising sun can flood the corpses with light, symbolizing the cycle of Life and Death. At Chullpas (An ancient funerary building for aristocrats). 📍 Lat -15.9668, Long -65.6557.

items.name: #9 Tinku
items.location: Legend · Just west of Panua Village · 📍 -15.4425, -65.7571
items.guide: Every year, rural communities in the region of Potosi organize big celebrations called Tinku: in daytime, the villagers brawl following special rites. Shedding blood is a way to honor the Earth goddess and ensure the promise of a good harvest. It is also a way to release social tensions. Clay pots such as this one are traditionally used to drink alcohol. The drunkest or toughest guys fight to the death. Even the women take part, helping their husbands or fighting each other. Just west of Panua Village (A remote village that lives in peace). 📍 Lat -15.4425, Long -65.7571.

items.name: #10 Wilancha
items.guide: La Wilancha is a sacrificial ritual to honor Pachamama, the Earth goddess. Indigenous people cut a llama's throat and shed its blood on the ground, hoping for a good harvest. Miners spill the blood over mine entrances for safety at work or to find a good vein of minerals. As Pachamama is a jealous goddess, the ritual is considered mandatory to satisfy her. During the Wilancha ceremony, a shaman or one of his aides may blow horns such as this one to attract Pachamama's good graces. At Sacrificial Site (Llamas are sacrificed here). 📍 Lat -15.9063, Long -65.6658.

items.name: #2 Klaus Barbie
items.location: Picture Evidence · At Klaus Barbie House · 📍 -13.2327, -62.4497
items.guide: Klaus Barbie is an infamous Nazi officer known for hunting members of the French Resistance and sending Jewish children to death camps during World War II. When the war was over, he started to work as a secret agent for the US and later had to escape to Bolivia. Once there, he started dealing guns and drugs, playing a key role in various military regimes. During the 1980's, he was finally extradited to France and sentenced to life for his crimes. He died in prison in 1991. At Klaus Barbie House (The home where the war criminal lived in hiding). 📍 Lat -13.2327, Long -62.4497.

items.name: #3 Vehicle Blessing
items.guide: Bolivian roads are very dangerous. It is common to take all kinds of vehicles to church for consecration, to bring about holy protection. The most frequently visited place is the cathedral of Copacabana, on the shores of Lake Titicaca: people gather there every Sunday while the priest leads the blessing ritual by pouring holy water on the decorated vehicles. At A Car Wreck (Remains of a car crash). 📍 Lat -13.4835, Long -60.5828.

items.name: #4 The Death Road
items.location: Legend · At Las Tumbas del Camino · 📍 -13.3944, -62.1773
items.guide: The Death Road is a 50 km road connecting La Paz to the northern tropical area of Yungas. Built in the 1930s, it soon turned into a major transit route. However, the slippery and narrow slope is considered one of the most dangerous roads in the world: an average of 200 people fall into the precipice each year, most of them truck drivers and bus passengers. A safer road was constructed, but the Death Road is still used by some old trucks and tourists. At Las Tumbas del Camino (Some victims of the Death Road are buried here). 📍 Lat -13.3944, Long -62.1773.

items.name: #10 Túpac Katari (1750-81)
items.guide: Born into a poor Aymara family, Túpac Katari led a major indigenous rebellion against the Spanish Empire between 1780 and 1781. Followed by 40,000 supporters, along with his wife Bartolina Sisa, he twice laid siege to La Paz against the Spanish. Subsequently betrayed, he was arrested, tortured, and finally quartered on the 15th of November 1781. Just before dying, he said: "I die, but I will return as millions." He is now considered an early martyr of the indigenous struggle. At Tupac Katari Tomb (Tomb of the 18th century Bolivian rebel). 📍 Lat -16.8017, Long -65.8231.

items.name: #11 Laguna Colorada
items.guide: Laguna Colorada, or Red Lagoon, is a shallow salt lake of some 60 square kilometers. It is located in southwestern Bolivia, in the Lípez area. Its peculiar color comes from a mix of red sediments and algae with white crystals of borax. The lagoon is an important mating site for pink flamingos. Local people traditionally come here to hunt them using bolas, a very effective kind of throwing weapon made of stones on the ends of interconnected cords that entangle the long legs of the flamingos. At Hunter Shelter (A flamingo hunters' shelter). 📍 Lat -17.4691, Long -66.3531.

items.name: #12 El Condor y la Cholita
items.guide: According to legend, a condor once fell in love with a young cholita, a native girl, and turned into a young man to seduce her. However, the distrustful mother of the girl intervened and threw boiling water on the condor, burning its head and neck. The bird had to fly away but grabbed the girl and took her to its nest. The young captive later managed to escape, with the help of a wise little bird. The condor was left sad and alone, now bald from the top of its head to its shoulders. At Condor Cairn (A stone mound dedicated to condors). 📍 Lat -18.4266, Long -65.6723.

items.name: #7 Mama Cocha
items.guide: Mama Cocha is a kind of sea goddess, invoked by sailors and fishermen for protection or to ensure good fishing. In Bolivia, she is linked to the rivers and the lakes of the Andes, especially Titicaca. She is sometimes referred to as the wife of Viracocha, the pre-Columbian god and creator of all things with whom she had two children: Inti, the Sun, Mama Killa, the Moon. Some stories add Pachamama to the family. At A Fisherman's House (A solitary lakefront house). 📍 Lat -15.8874, Long -62.5356.

items.name: #8 The Chaco War
items.location: Legend · Just north of Campo Ana · 📍 -17.8436, -62.6509
items.guide: Fought between Bolivia and Paraguay, the Chaco war is the last international conflict that took place in Latin America. From 1932 to 1935, both countries fought for the control of the Chaco, an unexplored and wild territory in Southeastern Bolivia. Nearly 100,000 men died, many of them from thirst and disease, due to the hostile conditions of the region. Bolivia's defeat inflicted a national trauma that led to major political and social changes in the country during the following decades. Just north of Campo Ana (The center of the cocaine-making community). 📍 Lat -17.8436, Long -62.6509.

items.name: #9 Pachamama Scars
items.guide: Pachamama, the Andean Earth goddess and keeper of fertility, is revered across Bolivia. Recently, in Ocoro, entire patches of forest and all life within them have inexplicably died. Locals claim that Pachamama is bleeding, leaving irreversible raw sores on the land that shall never heal. Environmental agencies suspect the damage is caused by chemical waste runoff from nearby cocaine labs set up by the Santa Blanca Cartel in Ocoro. At Pachamama Scars (The earth is poisoned here by the cocaine production). 📍 Lat -17.7335, Long -61.7191.

Unidad police then used this as an excuse to increase security around the site. At Riverine Checkpoint (Controls the traffic on the lakes). 📍 Lat -15.3212, Long -62.5442.

items.name: #6 Cost of Doing Business
items.location: Picture Evidence · Northeast of Alicia Town · 📍 -15.1767, -63.6555
items.guide: A Barvechos Bank check signed by Javier "Carzita" Vallardo to a respectable New-York Law firm. Most likely bribers to secure the construction of Agua Verde's Resort and Casino. Northeast of Alicia Town (Formerly a tourist town, occupied by the cartel). 📍 Lat -15.1767, Long -63.6555.

items.name: #7 Golden Book
items.guide: A note for Javier "Carzita" Vallardo left by Ricky Sandoval. It seems like Agent Sandoval might have gone a little too deep undercover in the cartel. At Kantuta Mansion (The house of a foreign associate of the cartel). 📍 Lat -14.5231, Long -63.1212.

items.name: #8 Money and Fame
items.guide: Javier "Carzita" Vallardo is featured on the cover of the latest issue of a famous international tabloid. The son of Mexican billionaire Gonzalo Vallardo, Carzita is acting as the respectable public face of the cartel. A jetsetter and role model for some, he attracts famous athletes, celebrities and politicians to Agua Verde Resort, facilitating collusion and expanding the soft power of the Santa Blanca Cartel. At Outpost (The hideout of a high-ranking cartel member). 📍 Lat -14.8291, Long -61.4507.

items.name: #9 Carzita's Photogram Post
items.location: Picture Evidence · At La Nube Blanca · 📍 -15.3219, -61.7615
items.guide: Carzita's latest selfie has over 340,000 likes and counting. The son of Mexican billionaire Gonzalo Vallardo. Javier "Carzita" Vallardo is acting as a role model, the respectable face of the cartel, expanding the soft power of Santa Blanca. At La Nube Blanca (A boat used as mobile cocaine laboratory). 📍 Lat -15.3219, Long -61.7615.

items.name: #10 Bolivia Buchon Blog
items.location: Picture Evidence · Just south of Buchon House · 📍 -15.1852, -63.0014
items.guide: In this blog post, Ramon Feliz condemns the opacity and blatant corruption that presided over the construction of Agua Verde's Resort and Casino. Just south of Buchon House (The house of a high-ranking member of the cartel). 📍 Lat -15.1852, Long -63.0014.

items.name: #11 The Legend of the Siren
items.guide: Elderly people living near the river banks and lake shores of Bolivia, whether on the Altiplano or in the lowlands, often tell stories about sirens. As the ones from ancient Greece, they are said to seduce the fishermen with their song in order to kill them. They allegedly disappeared a long time ago, but, from time to time, you can still read testimonies in Bolivian newspapers of people who saw sirens. At Siren Island (A desert island). 📍 Lat -14.8138, Long -63.194.

items.name: #1 DJ Perico
items.location: Bowman Briefing · Out in the open, south of Outpost · 📍 -18.1451, -63.8273
items.guide: This Kingslayer File unlocks automatically after Bowman's briefing upon entering Pucara for the first time. Wannabe tough guy, disc jockey for Santa Blanca Cartel Radio. Out in the open, south of Outpost (Controls the area). 📍 Lat -18.1451, Long -63.8273.

items.name: #2 El Sueño Narcocorrido
items.location: Recording · Just southeast of Todos Santos Town · 📍 -18.958, -64.1291
items.guide: Part of El Chido's album for Santa Blanca, this is the corrido for El Sueño. Just southeast of Todos Santos Town (The provincial capital and center of llama farming). 📍 Lat -18.958, Long -64.1291.

items.name: #3 El Tio
items.guide: An old-timer talks about how his sacrifice of a llama to El Tio de la Mina (Uncle of the Mine) saved him from a mine cave-in during which everyone else died. At Outpost (Storage of the cartel's gas in Pucara). 📍 Lat -18.6402, Long -64.423.

items.name: #4 On Air
items.location: Recording · Just northeast of Santa Muerte Tomb · 📍 -18.9912, -63.7825
items.guide: DJ Perico doesn't realize his sound engineer forgot to cut his mike at the end of his show and rants about the cartel. Just northeast of Santa Muerte Tomb (La Plaga's tomb, under construction). 📍 Lat -18.9912, Long -63.7825.

items.name: #5 The Fighter
items.guide: News piece on Tinku fighter Raul Vargas. Known as the Jaguar of the King, he strapped broken glass to his knuckles before fights. At Riverine Docks (Docks built by the cartel). 📍 Lat -18.8923, Long -64.8954.

items.name: #6 A Tomb for a King
items.location: Recording · Just southeast of Old Silver Mine · 📍 -19.4803, -63.8816
items.guide: DJ Perico has El Sueño on his show to reveal that the cartel is building a massive mausoleum. Just southeast of Old Silver Mine (An abandoned silver mine). 📍 Lat -19.4803, Long -63.8816.

items.name: #7 El Sueño's Mausoleum
items.location: Picture Evidence · Just southwest of Todos Santos Rock Quarry · 📍 -19.3523, -64.0641
items.guide: The blueprint of El Sueño's mausoleum project in Pucara. A mausoleum is a type of tomb, usually of grand proportions, built for historical figures such as kings or emperors. Just southwest of Todos Santos Rock Quarry (Stones to build the tombs are extracted here). 📍 Lat -19.3523, Long -64.0641.

items.name: #8 Perico Flyer
items.guide: The flyer for a special event in Pucara organized by DJ Perico At Pilca Mine (This zinc mine is exploited by OMZnA S.A). 📍 Lat -18.9971, Long -62.7292.

items.name: #9 Family Photo
items.location: Picture Evidence · North of Pucara Base · 📍 -18.6619, -63.5812
items.guide: A photograph of young DJ Perico and his brother Manolo, shot in Los Angeles at the end of the nineties. In an effort to raise the morale of cartel members, the elusive Mexican-American DJ has been broadcasting throughout Bolivia since Santa Blanca set foot in country. North of Pucara Base (The HQ for building the cartel's tombs). 📍 Lat -18.6619, Long -63.5812.

items.name: #10 El Tío de la Mina
items.location: Legend · Just north of Old Silver Mine · 📍 -19.4077, -63.8914
items.guide: A god of the Underworld, El Tío represents a major figure of the mining culture in Bolivia. His origins date back to a pre-Columbian Uru god called Wari. Miners often gather deep inside the mines, especially in Potosi, offering liquor, cigarettes and coca leaves to a statue of El Tío, in exchange for its protection. Those who fail to honor him may suffer death and injuries. He is usually represented as a mix of a devil and a goat, with very explicit male attributes. Just north of Old Silver Mine (An abandoned silver mine). 📍 Lat -19.4077, Long -63.8914.

items.name: #11 The Silver Mines
items.location: Legend · Just north of Todos Santos Town · 📍 -18.8888, -64.1663
items.guide: The silver mines of Bolivia have been exploited since the Spanish Conquest in the 16th century. The most famous of them is Cerro Rico, the Rich Mountain, in Potosi. The labor force was once composed of natives of African slaves. Working in extreme conditions, millions died extracting the precious metal. Despite a steep decline in activity in the past 40 years, theses miners are still exploited today, and miners remain a significant social and cultural component of Bolivia. Just north of Todos Santos Town (The provincial capital and center of llama farming). 📍 Lat -18.8888, Long -64.1663.

items.name: #12 The Mausoleum of Halicarnassus
items.location: Legend · Just south of Pucara Base · 📍 -18.7976, -63.6135
items.guide: The Mausoleum of Halicarnassus was an ancient burial monument erected on a hill overlooking the city of Halicarnassus (modern-day Bodrum, Turkey). Built by Queen Artemisia in 353 BC to honor her dead husband Mausolus, the building became one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Made of carved marble, it stood approximately 43 meters (140 feet) tall, dominating the city for over 17 centuries. It was later destroyed by an earthquake in the 14th century. Just south of Pucara Base (The HQ for building the cartel's tombs). 📍 Lat -18.7976, Long -63.6135.

items.name: #1 El Gato
items.guide: This Kingslayer File unlocks automatically after Bowman's briefing upon entering Remanzo for the first time. Manager of packaging, has survived more mortal injuries than Rasputin. Southwest of Poco (A potters' village, now used by the cartel). 📍 Lat -14.8907, Long -66.078.

items.name: #2 Stuffed Spuds
items.guide: A couple of Santa Blanca guys come up with a "genius" new way to smuggle drugs. At Observation Post (Oversees cartel activities). 📍 Lat -15.0321, Long -65.1036.

items.name: #3 The Death of a Mule
items.location: Picture Evidence · Just south of Marcavi · 📍 -15.0593, -65.4691
items.guide: A newspaper article about the death of a Bolivian national in Miami International Airport. Autopsy revealed he had fourteen bags of cocaine inside his stomach. Four of these bags burst, causing him to O.D. Just south of Marcavi (Potato-farming center now occupied by the cartel). 📍 Lat -15.0593, Long -65.4691.

items.name: #4 Local Delight
items.guide: The recipe for the Mechado de Cordero, a traditional Bolivian meal. At Las Mulas (Prospective human drug mules wait here). 📍 Lat -14.4253, Long -66.0185.

items.name: #5 X-Ray
items.location: Picture Evidence · Just east of Outpost · 📍 -15.1314, -65.6128
items.guide: A chest X-ray of a woman, showing bags of cocaine hidden inside her breasts. Santa Blanca uses mules to smuggle cocaine across the border, hiding drugs inside breast implants, fake pregnant bellies, or by getting locals to ingest up to fifteen bags of cocaine. Just east of Outpost (A relay for cartel vehicles and convoys). 📍 Lat -15.1314, Long -65.6128.

items.name: #6 Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid
items.guide: According to legend, after a long crime career in the US, the infamous outlaws Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid had to escape to South America, ending up in Bolivia. In 1908, two Americans robbed the miners' payroll, near the Uyuni mine. Both were killed by the Army. Locals are convinced that they were Butch and Sundance. Though no solid proof of this fact exists, the so-called tomb of Butch Cassidy can be seen in the San Vincente cemetery. At San Vicente (Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid's last stand). 📍 Lat -15.2501, Long -65.0634.

items.name: #7 Potatoes
items.guide: Potato crops are native to the Andes, somewhere between Peru and Bolivia. They have been cultivated and consumed by men for almost 10,000 years. More than 1,500 strands of potatoes exist in Bolivia, of all sizes, shapes, and colors, but only five can be found on the market. It is still a basic element of the Andean tradition and popular diet. At Buying Office (Local farmers sell their harvest here). 📍 Lat -14.9353, Long -65.4804.

items.name: #1 El Pozolero
items.location: Bowman Briefing · North of Sicario House · 📍 -15.4904, -63.9102
items.guide: This Kingslayer File unlocks automatically upon completing the story mission "The Death Truck". Mysterious and feared, he disposes of dead bodies for the cartel. North of Sicario House (Hunt the rebel agents). 📍 Lat -15.4904, Long -63.9102.

items.name: #2 Judgment Day
items.location: Recording · Just southeast of La Carcel Del Pueblo · 📍 -15.1036, -64.2908
items.guide: Judge Miguel Bardez makes one last call as the cartel targets him for daring to speak out against them. Just southeast of La Carcel Del Pueblo (Bolivian pro-rebels are imprisoned here). 📍 Lat -15.1036, Long -64.2908.

items.name: #3 La Cancion del Pozolero
items.guide: El Pozolero sings a Mexican nursery rhyme as he dissolves a dead body. Just southeast of Outpost (Communications center controlling the southern border). 📍 Lat -16.1992, Long -63.6867.

items.name: #4 El Pozolero Narcocorrido
items.location: Recording · Just southwest of Prison Rosario · 📍 -15.8936, -64.205
items.guide: Part of El Chido's album for Santa Blanca, this is the corrido for El Pozolero. Just southwest of Prison Rosario (Prison village housing cartel penitentiary administration). 📍 Lat -15.8936, Long -64.205.

items.name: #5 Dumb but Deadly
items.location: Recording · Just southwest of Makeshift Runway · 📍 -15.7512, -64.6144
items.guide: El Muro and La Plaga discuss their feelings on El Pozolero. Just southwest of Makeshift Runway (A runway improvised by the cartel). 📍 Lat -15.7512, Long -64.6144.

items.name: #6 Dead End
items.guide: Ramon Feliz tells his mother about the horrible things the cartel has made him do. She tries to convince him he only did it to protect their family. At San Mateo Base (The center of the counter insurrection in San Mateo). 📍 Lat -15.4252, Long -64.7791.

items.name: #7 Mass disappearances
items.guide: A Barvechos Newspaper article about the wave of disappearances hitting San Mateo. In this region, Santa Blanca has hit the rebels harder than anywhere in Bolivia, kidnapping entire families of suspected rebels and detaining them arbitrarily, sometimes for months. At Train Station (The San Mateo train station). 📍 Lat -15.0733, Long -64.7535.

items.name: #8 El Pozolero's Notebook
items.guide: El Pozolero deals in "waste management" for the cartel. At Boot Camp (Sicarios are trained here to fight the rebellion). 📍 Lat -15.4714, Long -64.158.

items.name: #9 Everyone can cook
items.location: Picture Evidence · North of San Mateo Base · 📍 -15.3355, -64.7953
items.guide: A delivery bound for chemical solvents. Possibly used to dissolve bones and flesh. North of San Mateo Base (The center of the counter insurrection in San Mateo). 📍 Lat -15.3355, Long -64.7953.

items.name: #10 Desaparecido
items.location: Picture Evidence · Just west of Makeshift Runway · 📍 -15.7274, -64.6158
items.guide: A Missing Person poster for Miguel Baradez, a judge that mysteriously disappeared in San Mateo. Any information on him may help the police. Just west of Makeshift Runway (A runway improvised by the cartel). 📍 Lat -15.7274, Long -64.6158.

items.name: #11 Pishtacos
items.guide: According to folklore, the Pishtaco is a kind of vampire or bogeyman, typically from the Andes. Described as a human-like figure with white skin and a pale face, he kidnaps lone travelers at night, sometimes killing them, in order to steal their body fat. Indeed, the body fat is important in the Andes because it is considered a sign of wealth and good health. Note that the Pishtaco's description is a clear reference to Spanish and other European settlers. At Abandoned House (The inhabitants mysteriously disappeared). 📍 Lat -15.3185, Long -64.5531.

items.name: #1 Madre Coca
items.guide: This Kingslayer File unlocks automatically after Bowman's briefing upon entering Tabacal for the first time. After a lifetime picking coca leaves, she manages the cartel's coca fields. Northeast of Cardoza (A coffee-farmer and cattle town). 📍 Lat -14.5892, Long -63.7877.

items.name: #2 It's Only Business
items.location: Recording · Just west of Tabacal Base · 📍 -13.3965, -63.3061
items.guide: El Muro voices doubts to El Sueño about making Madre Coca and El Yayo buchos. Just west of Tabacal Base (Coca from Tabacal and Monte Puncu is stored here). 📍 Lat -13.3965, Long -63.3061.

items.name: #3 Ghosts Narcocorrido
items.location: Recording · Just north of Killasisa Farm · 📍 -14.2904, -63.5429
items.guide: Part of El Chido's album for Santa Blanca, this is the corrido for (or rather, against) the Ghosts. Just north of Killasisa Farm (A traditional cocalero's family farm). 📍 Lat -14.2904, Long -63.5429.

items.name: #4 Market Economy
items.guide: El Yayo talks with Madre Coca about her promise to pay local farmers more for coca than any other crop, including coffee. If they don't see the generosity in her offer, she'll force them to take it anyhow. At Observation Post (Oversees the cartel's activities). 📍 Lat -14.0922, Long -62.9617.

items.name: #5 Rules & Regs
items.location: Picture Evidence · Just north of Secure Barn West · 📍 -13.8623, -63.6943
items.guide: A letter from the Coca Regulatory Board to the Cocalero Unions, setting the standard price for coca. In Bolivia, the price of coca leaves used to be government regulated. That was before Santa Blanca set foot in the country and disrupted market prices by buying massive amount of coca under the counter from local cocaleros. Just north of Secure Barn West (A barn where the cartel stores dried coca leaves). 📍 Lat -13.8623, Long -63.6943.

items.name: #6 Madre Coca Ex-Voto
items.location: Picture Evidence · Just southwest of Outpost · 📍 -13.4939, -62.4012
items.guide: An ex-votto is a symbolic offering made in churches in fulfillment of a vow or as an expression of devotion. This ex-votto was left by Madre Coca as a plea to heal her son. It didn't work, as he died a few weeks later. Just southwest of Outpost (Relay for the cartel's vehicles and convoys). 📍 Lat -13.4939, Long -62.4012.

items.name: #7 Treasure Map
items.location: Picture Evidence · At Secure Barn East · 📍 -14.1071, -62.0896
items.guide: A map of coca plantations and markets in the Tabacal region. In Bolivia, the area used to grow coca was regulated by Law 1008 in July of 1988. Twelve thousand hectares of legal cultivation were established to meet traditional demands. After Santa Blanca set foot in Bolivia, the area covered by illegal crops quickly grew to surpass the legal area. The current ratio is around 7 to 1. At Secure Barn East (A barn where the cartel stores dried coca leaves). 📍 Lat -14.1071, Long -62.0896.

items.name: #1 El Wey
items.location: Bowman Briefing · West of Villa Verde · 📍 -14.6103, -59.9798
items.guide: This Kingslayer File unlocks automatically after Bowman's briefing upon entering Villa Verde for the first time. In charge of the cartel's mining operation, he got his face burned off in a chemical accident. West of Villa Verde (The traditional capital of Bolivian coca trading). 📍 Lat -14.6103, Long -59.9798.

items.name: #2 A Local Feud
items.guide: A news report about riots between the cocaleros and the miners. Northwest of Maco (A cocalero village controlled by the cartel). 📍 Lat -16.1617, Long -61.1653.

items.name: #3 A Small Favor
items.guide: Since Via-B is not responding, Jensen asks El Wey for some of the chemicals he needs to process cocaine. El Wey agrees and offers to get the Via-B people in line, too. Just south of Palmeras (A fisherman village occupied by the cartel). 📍 Lat -16.3874, Long -60.1866.

items.name: #4 Union Negotiations
items.guide: El Yayo and El Wey discuss the demands of the mining collective. When El Wey threatens to replace them with Brazilians, El Yayo says he'll work it out with the locals. At Outpost (Protects the coca fields from rebel raids). 📍 Lat -15.19, Long -59.5714.

items.name: #5 El Boquita Narcocorrido
items.guide: Part of El Chido's album for Santa Blanca, this is the corrido for El Boquita. At Quya Farm (A traditional cocalero's family farm). 📍 Lat -14.6625, Long -59.2824.

items.name: #6 Market Hours
items.guide: A poster with the hours of the Coca Market of Villa Verde, one of the biggest in Bolivia. Between three and four thousands pounds of coca are sold daily in the La Paz coca market alone. At Makeshift Runway (A runway improvised by the cartel). 📍 Lat -15.2441, Long -59.9179.

items.name: #7 Vintage Horror
items.location: Picture Evidence · East of Villa Verde · 📍 -14.6158, -59.6009
items.guide: A poster for a budget horror movie shot in Mexico, inspired by the scarred face of El Wey, the buchon of Villa Verde. Strangely enough, the whole film crew went missing a few days after the film was released. East of Villa Verde (The traditional capital of Bolivian coca trading). 📍 Lat -14.6158, Long -59.6009.

items.name: #8 Bible Page - La Santera
items.location: Picture Evidence · South of Villa Verde · 📍 -14.7372, -59.7646
items.guide: The Santa Blanca Drug Cartel is writing its own version of the Bible. This is the page for La Santera, the High Priestess of Santa Muerte. South of Villa Verde (The traditional capital of Bolivian coca trading). 📍 Lat -14.7372, Long -59.7646.

items.name: #9 Diablada
items.guide: La Diablada is the Spanish name for the Devil's Carnival held each February in the mining city of Oruro to honor the Virgen del Socavón - the Virgin of the Tunnel - the saint patroness of miners. The carnival takes its name from one of its most emblematic dance, la Diablada, during which performers wear devil suits, masks and horns and parade in the streets. The dance dates back to the pre-Columbian period of the Urus who used to practice it in honor of the god Wari. At Villa Verde (The traditional capital of Bolivian coca trading). 📍 Lat -14.5845, Long -59.7555.

items.name: #10 Mama Coca
items.guide: Legends about Mama Coca often tell very different tales: some think she was Pachamama's daughter. Others say she was the courted wife of one of the first Incan emperors. But most stories end up with the idea that she died, her body was dismembered and buried separately. In the tomb's center appeared a new plant called "coca", whose leaves, originally reserved for men, could be used to relieve pains and soon were considered sacred. At Mama Coca Shrine (A shrine dedicated to an Inca goddess). 📍 Lat -16.2177, Long -59.9536.

items.name: #11 The Woman that Turned into a Tree
items.guide: According to an eastern myth, a beautiful girl once fell in love with a warrior and married him. One day, he went to war but never returned. His wife was so sad that she disappeared into the forest and died embracing a big, round tree. When some hunters found her, they could not take her back to the village because her body had become part of the tree. As time passed, she changed completely into a tree. The legend goes that once a year, a single flower blossoms on the bark of the tree. At Imaybe Glade (A legendary glade). 📍 Lat -14.9548, Long -59.2883.

collectible_types.description: The 5 main collectible types in the base game, roughly 400+ items across the 21 provinces. Tick a type once you've finished it.

items.name: Kingslayer Files (201)
items.guide: Lore, character backstories and Bolivian legends. Red icons are documents, audio logs, photos and videos; green icons are Legends; Mission Files come automatically when you first enter a province or beat its Buchón. They aren't revealed by intel caches. Get close or visit nearby ? locations to make them appear. Track each province in the Kingslayer Files section.

items.name: Weapons (80)
items.guide: 50 Weapon Cases (blue gun icons once you gather local intel) holding assault rifles, sniper rifles, SMGs, LMGs, shotguns and handguns, plus 30 pre-customized Boss Weapons unlocked automatically by defeating cartel bosses in the story. Exact names and locations are on MapGenie or the Steam Community collectibles guide.

items.name: Weapon Accessories (98)
items.guide: Scopes, extended magazines, barrels, stocks, underbarrel grips/grenade launchers and rail laser sights, in blue accessory cases revealed by regional intel caches. Not needed for any trophy or achievement.

items.name: Bonus Medals (26 base / 30 with DLC)
items.guide: Permanent passive upgrades (e.g. more explosives, faster revives, quieter running, bullet resistance, stronger rebel support). A medal only works once you've unlocked its matching base skill. Mark each one with the star on its skill in the skill tree sections. Each province holds one or two.

items.name: Skill Point Medals (149)
items.guide: Each pickup gives +1, +3 or +5 Skill Points. There are more in the world than you need to max every skill, so you can skip about 20 of them.

weapons_by_province.description: All 51 base-game Weapon Cases with what's nearby and Lat/Long, plus the province-linked Boss Weapons for defeating cartel targets. Tick each weapon once you have it.

items.name: MK-48

items.name: Mk 17

items.name: M40A5

items.name: Scorpion EVO 3
items.guide: A Czech SMG with a high rate of fire. Just northeast of Combat Outpost (Unidad road patrols start here). 📍 Lat -14.1341, Long -65.7301.

items.name: SR-1
items.guide: Police across Europe use this bolt-action bullpup. At El Buen Sal (An abandoned salt mine). 📍 Lat -14.3478, Long -67.2668.

items.name: SPAS-12

tips: Skills have between 1 and 4 ranks (Rebel Support skills have 3). Click a rank box to jump straight to that rank; click the already-active top box again to drop back one rank.
A skill with a Bonus Medal (shown as a star) has that medal as a separate, independent toggle from its tier boxes — the medal is a one-off map pickup, not another rank.
Rebel Support's Vehicle Drop-Off is the one skill with explicitly documented per-rank differences: Rank 1 calls an SUV, Rank 2 an armored vehicle, Rank 3 a helicopter.
The last column of the Weapon, Drone, Physical and Squad trees unlocks at player level 14, 15, 17 and 16. Rank counts and costs now come from the IGN / Ghost Recon Wiki skill lists.
Kingslayer Files: about 200 across the 21 base-game provinces (some count up to 203), from 4 in Monte Puncu to 14 in Koani. Operation Oracle adds 12 more.
Kingslayer Files don't show on your map until you get close to them or visit nearby locations and question marks (?), unlike Skill Points or weapon cases.
The Whole Story trophy only needs the collectible documents, not the mission-granted 'Word of Sueno' videos. If your count looks stuck, check TrueAchievements for tracking-bug fixes.

Reveal collectibles fast: in every new province, grab the white ! intel (files, laptops or lieutenant interrogations). That reveals all the blue collectibles (Weapons, Accessories, Bonus Medals and Skill Points) on the province map.
Fly or drive through every unvisited ? location in a province to make the nearby red and green Kingslayer Files pop up on your mini-map.
You can skip about 20 Skill Point pickups and still max out the whole skill tree. Weapon accessories aren't needed for any trophy.
Yellow-file intel unlocks a story mission. White ! intel lets you pick what to reveal on the Tacmap: Skill Points, Equipment Cases, Bonus Medals, Supply Raids or Rebel Ops.
On the Tacmap, press Interact over a province to see the Kingslayer Files you've found and play their videos and audio.
Supply Raids (Steal the Helicopter, Steal the Plane, Stop the Convoy) give far more resources than containers; convoys give the most.
Skill trophies: Ultimate Skill (buy every upgrade in one tree), Top Drone (every drone upgrade), Only the Best (every upgrade), The Champion (max XP and level).

play_better.title: Play better: recommended
tips: Spend Skill Points on the cheap early ranks first (1 SP each) across Physical, Weapon and Drone trees before chasing the 4 SP ranks.
Drone first: the Drone tree (range, marking, battery) makes every outpost easier because you can tag guards and supplies before you move.
Tag supplies with the drone or binoculars as you go. Tagged Gasoline, Medication, Comms and Food are what pay for the higher skill ranks.
In co-op, split roles: one person on sniper plus Stable Aim and Stealth, the other on assault plus Squad skills like sync shots.
Run a suppressor on your primary for stealth, and keep a pistol suppressed for cleaning up lone guards without alerting the camp.
Do Rebel Support skills early: vehicle drop-off and reinforcements save a lot of driving and let you reset a mission quickly.
Mark Unidad and Santa Blanca outposts from a distance, take out alarms and commanders first, then clear the rest.
